provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — inbound weaponized Office/archive attachments are observable at the mail gateway and endpoint (attachment type, macro presence, SFX execution), but lure content and sender infrastructure are largely off-endpoint and require mail-security correlation
medium — user execution of an SFX/document dropper is detectable via process-creation lineage (Office/SFX spawning child processes, writes to temp) but depends on endpoint telemetry and baselining

high — Office application spawning child processes and writing/executing a dropped file (fwupdate.temp) on document close is a high-fidelity macro-execution signal via process-lineage and Office child-process telemetry
high — VBA macro activity is capturable via VBA/AMSI and Office macro logging, and the resulting file-drop-and-execute chain is observable in process telemetry

high — creation/modification of HKCU/HKLM Run keys pointing to loader binaries in user-writable paths is directly observable via registry-modification auditing (Sysmon EID 13) and autostart baselining
high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational); a task launching helper.exe from a user-writable path is a strong, specific detection candidate
medium — new service installation (Event ID 7045) for an unknown binary is detectable via service-install telemetry but requires baselining to separate from legitimate software

high — rundll32.exe loading a DLL from a non-standard user-writable path (SnailDriver directory) with an unusual export is detectable via process-creation command-line and module-load (Sysmon EID 7) telemetry
medium — DLL hijack/side-load is detectable via module-load telemetry and signature/path anomalies, but requires image-load instrumentation and baselining of legitimate DLL search paths
medium — filename/extension masquerading and decoy files are detectable via file-name/extension anomaly and MOTW/attachment inspection, but overlap with benign content
medium — filesystem/registry probing of AV product paths and enumeration of security products is detectable via file-access and process-behavior telemetry, but is subtle and needs correlation
medium — password-protected/encrypted archive creation and high-entropy dropped files are detectable via file-entropy and archive-utility telemetry, but require dedicated scanning
medium — keylogging hooks are hard to see directly, but the created keystroke-log artifact files and their staging/exfiltration are detectable via file-write and process-behavior telemetry
medium — screenshot capture leaves image artifacts written to disk that, together with process behavior, are detectable via file-write telemetry and screen-capture API monitoring where instrumented
medium — microphone-access and recorded-audio file artifacts are detectable via file-write telemetry and audio-device API monitoring where available
medium — access to browser credential stores (Login Data / logins.json / vault files) is detectable via file-access and process telemetry when browser credential-store paths are monitored
medium — reads of browser cookie databases are detectable via file-access telemetry on known cookie-store paths, correlated with the collecting process
medium — targeted document collection by extension is detectable via file-access patterns and staging behavior, but blends with legitimate file usage without process-lineage correlation
medium — automated, periodic collection produces recurring file-write and staging patterns detectable via behavioral analytics, but requires baselining
medium — creation of password-protected staging archives before egress is detectable via file-write and archive-utility telemetry, especially when correlated with subsequent C2 upload
medium — archive creation with password protection preceding network egress is detectable via process command-line and file-write telemetry

high — periodic HTTP(S) beaconing (fixed ~5-minute interval, POST to actor domains/IPs, signature-file fetch) is detectable via proxy/DNS/network telemetry and beacon-interval analytics, and pairs with the actor's C2 domain/IP IOCs

high — DGA-style lookups (short random-hex .space/.site/.win domains, high NXDOMAIN rates, low-reputation newly-registered domains) are detectable via DNS analytics and are a strong hunt-to-detect pivot for this actor
medium — self-signed/anomalous TLS certificates and signature-file fetches over HTTPS are detectable via TLS/JA3 fingerprinting and certificate-anomaly analytics, but require TLS-metadata visibility
medium — staged payload download following an initial beacon is detectable via file-write-after-network-download correlation and proxy telemetry, but depends on endpoint+network visibility
medium — outbound POST bodies of collected data to actor C2 are detectable via egress-volume anomalies and DLP/proxy correlation with the beaconing process, especially against known C2 IOCs
high — outbound FTP from a workstation to external servers (the actor's FTP IPs) is anomalous in most enterprises and detectable via network/proxy telemetry and egress-policy monitoring

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — in-memory window-enumeration and environment checks leave little discrete host telemetry; hunt candidate via memory/behavioral analysis rather than event logs
low — window enumeration is an in-process API behavior with minimal log footprint; hunt/behavioral candidate only
low — runtime string decoding is in-memory and largely invisible to standard logs; hunt candidate via memory/YARA analysis
low — clipboard reads are a common API with negligible log footprint; hunt candidate via behavioral correlation with keylog artifacts
low — removable-media enumeration is a common OS behavior with weak signal; hunt candidate via correlation with subsequent file collection from removable volumes
low — host-profiling API calls are common and low-signal; hunt candidate, meaningful mainly when correlated with beacon activity
low — process enumeration is ubiquitous and low-fidelity; hunt candidate only in tight process-lineage windows
low — locale/keyboard-language queries are benign OS calls with negligible detection value; hunt/behavioral only
low — certificate/key provisioning happens off-victim on adversary infrastructure; intel/hunt candidate via certificate-transparency and infrastructure tracking
low — encoded C2 content is opaque without deep protocol/decoder analysis; hunt candidate via traffic-pattern and decoder-based inspection
